text: Git branching is an important part of the version control workflow. When developers work on a new feature, they create a separate feature branch instead of changing the main code directly. This keeps the main branch stable and safe. Each developer can work independently on their own branch without affecting others. When the feature is ready, they merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often use pull requests to review the changes and discuss them. This process helps catch mistakes early and improves code quality. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can work faster and more organized.
